subject: Cloud Computing
title: Disaster Recovery Strategies
description: A quick win: understand Disaster Recovery Strategies.

hook.text: An entire AWS region goes down. Your application is only in that region. Everything stops.

buildup.text: Disaster recovery strategies range from backup-restore (cheapest, slowest) to active-active (expensive, instant).

discovery.text: Pilot light keeps a minimal copy ready. Warm standby keeps a scaled-down version running. Both balance cost and speed.

twist.text: Most companies choose backup-restore and accept hours of downtime. Active-active costs 2-3x but recovers in seconds.

climax.text: The right strategy depends on your recovery time objective. How long can your business survive being offline?

punchline.text: Faster recovery costs more. Know what downtime costs you.

quiz.question: What determines which disaster recovery strategy is appropriate?
options: How long the business can survive being offline (recovery time objective)
The number of employees in the company
Which cloud provider the company uses

details.summary: Cloud disaster recovery strategies range from backup-and-restore to multi-region active-active, each trading cost for recovery speed. Key metrics are RTO, the time to recover, and RPO, the acceptable data loss window. The right strategy depends on business criticality.
details.whyItMatters: Every cloud application will eventually face a failure. Choosing the right DR strategy ensures the business can recover within acceptable time and data loss limits.
takeaways: RTO measures recovery time, RPO measures acceptable data loss
Strategies range from cheap backup-restore to costly active-active
Multi-region deployments offer the fastest recovery

faq.question: What are the four DR strategy tiers?
faq.answer: Backup and restore is cheapest with the longest recovery. Pilot light keeps minimal infrastructure running. Warm standby runs a scaled-down copy of the full environment. Active-active runs full capacity in multiple regions with near-zero downtime.

faq.question: How often should disaster recovery be tested?
faq.answer: At least quarterly for critical systems. Automated DR drills through chaos engineering tools can test more frequently. Untested DR plans often fail when needed because assumptions about recovery procedures prove incorrect under real conditions.
